videos.description:
Ranked choice voting came to San Francisco in 2004. Today, 7 California cities use RCV.

After two decades in the Golden State, what’s the impact of RCV?

Our new report shows it has delivered better representation, better campaigns, & taxpayer savings.

Avram Reisman explains. 

Learn more about RCV in California at @calrcv  and read the report at the link in our bio! #RankedChoiceVoting

videos.title: Ezra Klein on How to Make Politicians Work Harder for Your Vote
videos.description:
Ezra Klein of the @EzraKleinShow  explains why he supports proportional representation in a conversation with Lee Drutman:

videos.description:
The gerrymandering war won’t end in 2026.

Stitch ➡️ @BetchesNews 

Ben McKenzie is right: Our country increasingly feels “winner-take-all.” Power & wealth concentrate at the top, while most Americans feel ignored & left behind.

One part of the problem? Winner-take-all elections.

The solution: Proportional representation.

videos.description:
As Mayor of Oakland, Libby Schaaf saw ranked choice voting push candidates to reach all voters – not just a narrow base.

videos.title: CLIP: Nick Troiano Talks 'Meaningful Votes' on CNN
videos.description: Does your vote really matter? Nick Troiano, Executive Director of Unite America, shares startling new findings like this: Only 14% of Americans elected the entire U.S. House of Representatives in 2024. In nearly 9 of every 10 elections in America, we know the outcome well in advance of a single vote being cast. The cure? In states with open primaries, the number of meaningful votes is nearly double when compared to states with closed primaries. Learn more from Nick in this short clip.

videos.title: Common Sense
videos.description:
Over 63% of Alaskans have chosen not to register with any political party.

And those voters don't slip through the cracks or get shunted to the sidelines.

Because Alaskans use open primaries and ranked choice voting to ensure every voter is heard clearly, regardless of party.

Voters are more than their political affiliation.

Alaskans know it.

That's why Alaska has open primaries and ranked choice voting, to ensure the power is held by the voters, not political parties.
